elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor"
"Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term."
"upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice" — shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "Customer shall have no further liability, early-termination charge, or penalty" — no fee mechanic (more favourable to Customer, but not the fallback bargain)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a term" — no end-of-term 90-day Vendor right granted

offending_extra_words: and Customer shall have no further liability, early-termination charge, or penalty
reasons: All four atomic elements of the preferred position are expressly met: a Customer convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a term.

The fallback is a separate bargain and is not satisfied (30 days rather than 60–90; no 3-month early-termination fee cap; no end-of-term Vendor right) — this is immaterial because the locked preferred level is complete.

Minimality is not fully satisfied: "and Customer shall have no further liability, early-termination charge, or penalty" adds a broad liability waiver not required by the preferred position, and "in whole or in part" expands scope beyond the position; the refund sentence alone would suffice.

The broad "no further liability" language sits in slight tension with Customer's obligation to pay Fees accrued before the effective date of termination and should be trimmed to "no early-termination charge or penalty" if raised.
Insertion as new 9.4 between 9.3 and 9.5 leaves surrounding termination and cumulative-remedies language untouched; no undefined terms introduced ("Fees", "Order Form" are defined).
